destination.title: Symmetries, charges and gauge consistency
destination.question: How do symmetry structures, charged objects and topological operators organize field theories and constrain their coupling to gravity?
destination.summary: The original packet supplies candidate membership rather than a scientific region statement. Its strongest common scope concerns symmetry definitions, charge completeness, gauge structure and their dynamical or gravitational consequences. Global gluing, network evolution, variational integrability and emergent gravitational dynamics remain accessible as neighboring questions. This region is a new proposal requiring independent review.

systems: Quantum field theories, including ordinary gauge theories and generalized symmetry constructions
String/M-theory, supergravity and specified quantum-gravity settings
Symmetry-compatible actions, solitons and duality constructions
targets: Symmetry definitions, operators, currents and anomalies
Charge sectors, completeness and gauge-group global structure
Gauging, explicit or spontaneous breaking, and infrared phases
Conditions and limitations of proposed quantum-gravity restrictions
regimes: Dimensions, asymptotics and effective limits remain source-specific
Finite, continuous, invertible and non-invertible structures remain distinguishable
Ordinary and pre-Swampland questions remain eligible
assumptions: Absence of global symmetries and charge completeness are investigated claims, not family-wide premises
Restrictions in known string constructions do not automatically exclude every other quantum-gravity completion
conventions: Gauge redundancy, physical global symmetry and gauge-group global form are distinct
Genuine probes, dynamical objects, endability and topologicality are distinguished
Form-degree conventions are retained separately where sources differ
includes: Related questions may share an overview without sharing a fine identity
Compound source questions retain their exact source-scoped access
Neighboring construction and emergence questions retain alternate homes
excludes: Treating numerical membership or source-object relations as scientific implications
Identifying every topological operator with an ordinary invertible global symmetry
Treating arbitrary global gluing, covariance or conserved topology as sufficient evidence of the narrower symmetry questions

sources.title: Symmetries and Strings in Field Theory and Gravity

evidence.text: How do discrete gauge theories, observable line and surface operators, and cosmic-string charges organize arguments about global symmetries, gauge-group compactness, charge completeness, and consistent supergravity couplings?

sources.title: Discrete gauge symmetries in D-brane models

evidence.text: Can phenomenologically useful discrete gauge symmetries arise directly as Stückelberg remnants in D-brane compactifications, protect dangerous operators against instantons, and realize R-parity, baryon triality, or their generalizations without selecting special scalar VEVs?

sources.title: A Chern-Simons Pandemic

evidence.text: When do the long-range fields of wrapped electrically charged objects prevent those objects from breaking a gauge-potential period symmetry?

sources.title: Exploring 2-Group Global Symmetries

evidence.text: How do continuous 2-group global symmetries constrain four-dimensional QFT current algebras, background fields, symmetry breaking, RG flows and ’t Hooft anomalies?

sources.title: Higher-form symmetries and spontaneous symmetry breaking

evidence.text: How do Goldstone modes, boundary conditions, gauge fixing, and dimensional obstructions to spontaneous symmetry breaking generalize to continuous higher-form symmetries?

sources.title: Symmetries in quantum field theory and quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can AdS/CFT establish the absence of internal global symmetries, completeness of gauge representations, and compactness of gauge groups, including discrete and higher-form cases?

sources.title: Differential cohomology and topological actions in physics

evidence.text: How can differential cohomology systematically construct topological actions with global or gauge symmetries, and detect obstructions to gauging global symmetries?

sources.title: Chern-Weil global symmetries and how quantum gravity avoids them

evidence.text: How are global symmetries generated by gauge-field characteristic forms removed in quantum gravity, and what does their removal imply for Chern-Simons couplings, localized fields, brane interactions, and axions?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Does the absence of magnetic global symmetry ensure a substantive magnetic completeness condition when gauging has already removed every genuine ’t Hooft operator?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: How does promoting the electromagnetic θ angle to a periodic dynamical axion change generalized symmetries, genuine probe operators and the endability of charged lines?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: How is a gauge vortex specified without introducing a dynamical vortex field?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Can magnetic objects required to break generalized symmetries arise inside a conventional Lagrangian gauge theory?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: How can charged states count toward completeness in a confining theory, where all infinite-volume asymptotic particles are neutral?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: How can a probe particle measure nonabelian vortex holonomy in a gauge-invariant way?

sources.title: Gravitational Solitons and Completeness

evidence.text: How do charged gravitational solitons change the relation between absence of global symmetries and completeness of gauge charges? Can topology supply the charges otherwise detected by non-invertible symmetries, leaving only a group-like obstruction to completeness?

sources.title: Non-invertible symmetries from discrete gauging and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: How does gauging charge conjugation change electric 1-form and dual (d−2)-form symmetries, and do proposed string embeddings supply defects that break the latter, consistently with the conjectured absence of global symmetries in quantum gravity?

sources.title: Generalized symmetries and Noether’s theorem in QFT

evidence.text: What obstructs the existence of local conserved currents for continuous QFT symmetries when localized symmetry implementers still exist, and how does this explain and generalize the Weinberg–Witten obstruction?

sources.title: Spinor-Vector Duality and the Swampland

evidence.text: How do symmetries of exact string vacua constrain their effective field theory limits, and can their complete symmetry structure suggest fundamental principles of quantum gravity?

sources.title: A fresh view on string orbifolds

evidence.text: Can string orbifolding be formulated through spacetime gauge symmetries and consistency conditions, treating all dynamical objects equally, despite the conjectural absence of global symmetries in quantum gravity? Can its possible outcomes be independent of duality frame?

sources.title: Duality origami: Emergent ensemble symmetries in holography and Swampland

evidence.text: The paper asks how averaging over boundary theories can produce global symmetries in a gravitational dual while remaining compatible with proposed quantum-gravity constraints and an underlying microscopic string description.

sources.title: Generalized Symmetries in Supergravities and Superconformal Field Theories via String Theory

evidence.text: How can string geometry and generalized symmetries constrain supergravity gauge-group topology and construct SCFT symmetry structures, twisted compactifications and duality defects?

sources.title: Generalized symmetries, gravity, and the swampland

evidence.text: How does coupling geometrically engineered QFT sectors to gravity gauge or break their generalized global symmetries, correlate polarizations, and determine the global gauge group?

sources.title: On the holographic dual of a topological symmetry operator

evidence.text: What bulk object represents a boundary topological symmetry operator, and can reconstruction explain its metric dependence and the absence of bulk global symmetries without initially assuming bulk gauging?

sources.title: Higher-group global symmetry and the bosonic M5 brane

evidence.text: How can continuous higher-group symmetry organize Goldstone effective theories and their thermal phases, explain bosonic D/M-brane fields, and accommodate the nonlinear self-duality of the M5 worldvolume field strength?

sources.title: Frozen generalized symmetries

evidence.text: How does fractional C3 holonomy freeze M-theory ADE gauge degrees of freedom, and how can identical asymptotic geometries support different generalized symmetries?

sources.title: (−1)-form symmetries from M-theory and SymTFTs

evidence.text: How do finite and continuous (−1)-form symmetries, their mixed anomalies, polarization choices and topological generators arise from M-theory geometric engineering?

sources.title: Decompactification Limits of Non-Compact Gauge Theory

evidence.text: Can an uncountable continuum of charged fields remove the global symmetries obstructing noncompact R gauge theory, and can the resulting lower-dimensional EFT instead acquire a consistent higher-dimensional interpretation?

sources.title: Generalised Symmetries and Swampland-Type Constraints from Charge Quantisation via Rational Homotopy Theory

evidence.text: How does a charge-quantisation homotopy type A encode brane charges and generalised symmetries, and what consistency constraints follow for field theories and quantum gravity?

sources.title: String probes, simple currents, and the no global symmetries conjecture

evidence.text: How does the worldsheet CFT of a faithful string encode the global form of a bulk gauge group, and can modular consistency explain why center one-form symmetries must be broken or gauged?

sources.title: Quantum groups in the Higgs phase

evidence.text: How do finite residual gauge symmetries organize the charges, fluxes, fusion and braiding of a Higgs phase, and why does Higgs screening remove Coulomb interactions while preserving Aharonov–Bohm interactions?

sources.title: Symmetries and Strings in Field Theory and Gravity

evidence.text: Use Wilson lines and surfaces, linking phases, and defect operators defined by excising neighborhoods and imposing flux or homotopy boundary conditions. These describe possible ultraviolet objects without requiring them to be dynamical in every field theory.

sources.title: Discrete gauge symmetries in D-brane models

evidence.text: For F-theory, derive C4∧FA∧FA couplings using the M-theory C3∧G4∧G4 term, then reduce magnetic fluxes to BF coefficients. Split spectral-cover bundles and their first Chern classes organize the surviving U(1)X and its flux.

sources.title: Antisymmetric tensor $Z_p$ gauge symmetries in field theory and string theory

evidence.text: Dimensionally reduce higher-dimensional Chern–Simons couplings in quantized flux backgrounds. For torsion examples, expand gauge potentials on nonclosed forms whose derivatives contain the integer p.

sources.title: A Chern-Simons Pandemic

evidence.text: Impose a periodic-scalar winding condition, reduce its kinetic term with the KK connection, and identify the induced covariant derivative. Treat changing the winding sector separately from varying continuous fields within one sector.

sources.title: Exploring 2-Group Global Symmetries

evidence.text: Current Ward identities are analyzed through momentum-space Lorentz decompositions and Bose symmetry. Characteristic three-point functions are simplified at p²=q²=(p+q)²=Q²; polynomial contact terms are distinguished from nonanalytic contributions.

sources.title: Higher-form symmetries and spontaneous symmetry breaking

evidence.text: Poincare duality, relative homology, and Hodge decomposition organize charges, boundary-preserving gauge transformations, and the gauge condition d†A=f. Higher p requires a tower of gauge-of-gauge fixing and ghosts.

sources.title: Duality symmetric actions

evidence.text: Can dual potentials coexist in an action with their duality relation imposed dynamically, making electric-magnetic symmetries manifest while retaining Lorentz and general coordinate invariance through nonstandard transformations?

sources.title: Reflections on Parity Breaking

evidence.text: Can fundamental gauged parity, spontaneously broken by low-energy dynamics, produce stable cosmological walls despite the additional defects required by quantum gravity?

sources.title: From global symmetries to local currents: The Free U(1) case in 4 dimensions

evidence.text: Can local generators of global internal symmetries be constructed from local implementations of the flip on a doubled theory, and can conserved Wightman currents be recovered by shrinking the generators' localization regions to a point?

sources.title: Holographic Duals of Symmetry Broken Phases

evidence.text: Can a continuous-symmetry SymTFT, after gauging a suitable Lagrangian algebra and choosing dynamical boundary conditions, serve as a gravity dual of the universal EFT for spontaneous symmetry breaking, including anomalies, higher groups and non-invertible symmetries?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Does a theory with a complete inventory of dynamical endpoints have no nontrivial topological operators, and conversely? The authors pose this broader equivalence beyond their proved Wilson, Gukov-Witten and vortex-sector statements.

sources.title: Symmetry and Emergence

evidence.text: How should gauge and global symmetries be understood across particle physics, condensed matter, and quantum gravity, especially when particles, gauge descriptions, and spacetime may emerge?

sources.title: A Panorama Of Physical Mathematics c. 2022

evidence.text: Which mathematical frameworks can define QFT and string/M-theory, organize their protected sectors and symmetries, and translate physical consistency into geometry, topology and number theory? This is a forward-looking research panorama.

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Can generic representation types distinguish quotient and direct-product global forms of the standard-model group?

sources.title: Topological Operators and Completeness of Spectrum in Discrete Gauge Theories

evidence.text: What replaces the proposed equivalence between electric completeness and absence of electric one-form symmetry for finite nonabelian gauge groups, and what might the replacement imply for quantum gravity?

sources.title: Beyond Standard Models and Grand Unifications: Anomalies, Topological Terms, and Dynamical Constraints via Cobordisms

evidence.text: Which spacetime/internal structure describes a GUT with spinorial matter, and how does allowing gauge-invariant fermionic operators affect that structure?

sources.title: The anomaly that was not meant IIB

evidence.text: Which duality symmetry and field transformations survive charge quantization in the low-energy type IIB description?

sources.title: The universal C*-algebra of the electromagnetic field II. Topological charges and spacelike linear fields

evidence.text: Under what conditions can regular representations of the universal electromagnetic algebra carry nontrivial topological charges? Determine the roles of test-function linearity, electric currents, and multiple electromagnetic species.

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Can missing dynamical charged objects be diagnosed by topological operators? The window compares electric particles, magnetic objects and twist vortices, allowing compact gauge groups with disconnected components and distinguishing endability from topologicality.

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: What monodromies occur when a discrete gauge transformation changes a continuous charge or permutes entire gauge sectors?

sources.title: Domain wall seeds in CSO-gauged supergravity

evidence.text: Does vanishing gauge-group Noether charge ensure that every consistent scalar–metric domain-wall flow can be generated from a diagonal coset-matrix seed by one global transformation independent of the transverse coordinate?

sources.title: Automatic enhancement in 6D supergravity and F-theory models

evidence.text: When does a gauge group and anomaly-compatible matter spectrum require additional gauged symmetry in a quantum-gravity construction? The proposed criterion compares the desired theory with a containing theory whose additional symmetry cannot be removed by a supersymmetric Higgs deformation.

sources.title: ICTP lectures on (non-)invertible generalized symmetries

evidence.text: How can generalized internal symmetries be described by topological defects, constructed through gauging, and related to extended charges and the Symmetry TFT?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: How can representation fine tuning be quantified while holding the gauge symmetry fixed?

sources.title: Universal Non-Invertible Symmetries

evidence.text: Which universal dual symmetries arise upon gauging a finite generalized symmetry, beyond Wilson defects, and how do their surface, interface and junction structures relate to condensation defects and disconnected gauge groups?

sources.title: SymTh for non-finite symmetries

evidence.text: Can a weakly coupled, non-topological bulk symmetry theory encode a boundary QFT's non-finite generalized symmetries, including non-flat backgrounds, dynamical gauging, anomalies and non-invertible defects?

sources.title: Continuous Global Symmetries and Hyperweak Interactions in String Compactifications

evidence.text: How do arguments excluding exact continuous global symmetries extend to D-branes, and how can approximate flavour symmetries and hyperweak gauge interactions nevertheless arise in four-dimensional effective theories?

sources.title: Spectrum generating symmetries for BPS solitons

evidence.text: Can actual symmetries generate physically distinct BPS solitons with different masses at fixed scalar vacuum, and can that spectrum-generating structure survive charge quantization and quantum corrections?

sources.title: Generalized symmetry in dynamical gravity

evidence.text: Does nonlinear dynamical gravity admit an electric one-form symmetry analogous to Yang–Mills center symmetry, and what are its charged operators, geometric defects, and conditions for explicit breaking?

sources.title: P-brane dyons and electric magnetic duality

evidence.text: What charge-quantization rules and electric–magnetic duality properties hold for dyons coupled to self-interacting Abelian p-form fields, and why does the relative sign of the quantization condition depend on p parity even without duality invariance?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Can an incomplete gauge-charge spectrum be detected by topological operators even when ordinary higher-form symmetry is absent? Disconnected and finite nonabelian gauge groups require a broader diagnostic than the center symmetry familiar from connected gauge theories.

sources.title: A Chern-Simons Pandemic

evidence.text: Can topology sums remove period symmetries in every compactification, or are independent Chern–Simons mechanisms necessary? The source also proposes examining boundary anomalies and non-abelian isometries as routes to further examples.

sources.title: Symmetry protected entanglement renormalization

evidence.text: Can enforcing symmetry on individual MERA tensors produce an RG flow with distinct fixed points for symmetry-protected phases, and explicitly realize a global boundary symmetry as a local symmetry of the bulk tensor network?

sources.title: Fate of stringy noninvertible symmetries

evidence.text: Which non-invertible gauge symmetries can occur in quantum gravity, how do worldsheet topology and string tension affect them, and what can their approximate survival imply for towers of states and Swampland constraints?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Can continuous-group Higgsing define genericity for discrete gauge groups?

sources.title: Massive Kaluza-Klein theories and their spontaneously broken symmetries

evidence.text: Which spontaneously broken gauge symmetries permit consistent massive Kaluza–Klein spin-3/2 and spin-2 couplings, and can their lower-dimensional actions be constructed by gauging an unbroken phase?

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: Generalized Symmetries in Quantum Field Theory and Beyond

evidence.text: How do generalized global symmetries and their anomalies constrain QFT dynamics, especially renormalization group flows, confinement, and possible infrared phases?

sources.title: Constraints on Symmetries from Holography

evidence.text: Can nonperturbative AdS/CFT establish the conjectured absence of global symmetries, completeness of internal gauge representations, and compactness of internal gauge groups, using definitions that distinguish physical symmetries from gauge redundancy?

sources.title: Beyond Standard Models and Grand Unifications: Anomalies, Topological Terms, and Dynamical Constraints via Cobordisms

evidence.text: Could a global anomaly of a specified visible-sector theory require additional infrared structure with phenomenological consequences?

sources.title: On completeness and generalized symmetries in quantum field theory

evidence.text: Can completeness be formulated for QFT without first assuming symmetries, weak coupling or particular operators, and how does failure of completeness determine generalized symmetries and their dual partners?

sources.title: Generalized Global Symmetries

evidence.text: Formulate higher-form global symmetries intrinsically through extended operators, and determine their consequences for selection rules, gauging, duality, spontaneous breaking, anomalies and phases of quantum field theory.

sources.title: Swampland constraints on the symmetry topological field theory of supergravity

evidence.text: Which choices of gauge-group global structure, apparently admissible for an absolute field theory, survive coupling to quantum gravity? Can restrictions from compact string/M-theory geometries be characterized through SymTFT boundary conditions?

sources.title: Quantifying non-invertible chiral symmetry breaking

evidence.text: Can effective charges q(r), previously used for continuous invertible higher-form symmetries, quantify explicit breaking of ABJ-like non-invertible symmetries, particularly the chiral symmetry of massless QED coupled to a massive scalar?

sources.title: Lectures on generalized symmetries

evidence.text: How are invertible generalized global symmetries defined and computed in QFT, and how do anomalies, gauging, spontaneous breaking and higher-group structures organize gauge-theory physics?

sources.title: Monopoles, duality, and string theory

evidence.text: Does a framework that requires electric charge quantization also require magnetic monopoles, and should a fully unified theory supply a maximal lattice of electric and magnetic charges for every gauge field?

sources.title: Solitonic Symmetry beyond Homotopy: Invertibility from Bordism and Noninvertibility from Topological Quantum Field Theory

evidence.text: Does homotopy classification correctly determine solitonic symmetries when solitons of different dimensions coexist, and what replaces the apparent hopfion U(1) symmetry of the four-dimensional CP¹ model?

sources.title: Metric isometries, holography, and continuous symmetry operators

evidence.text: What bulk objects realize continuous boundary symmetry operators arising from internal metric isometries, and how can their tension, geometry, worldvolume topological terms, and interactions with other symmetry operators be determined?

sources.title: Heterotic Effective Action and Duality Symmetries Revisited

evidence.text: Which continuous duality symmetries survive in the massless heterotic effective action when the full non-abelian gauge sector is retained, to all orders in α′, and how can the surviving symmetry be displayed explicitly?

sources.title: Discrete anomaly matching

evidence.text: Which additional necessary constraints do unbroken discrete global symmetries impose on proposed infrared spectra and gauge dualities beyond continuous ’t Hooft anomaly matching?

sources.title: Symmetry topological field theory for flavor symmetry

evidence.text: How can non-abelian BF theory encode continuous flavor symmetry, flat-connection gauging, the resulting dual symmetry, and anomalies, including an explicit construction of operators acting non-abelianly on boundary local operators?

destination.title: Higher-derivative interactions, supersymmetry and duality
destination.question: How do supersymmetry, duality and consistency constrain higher-derivative gravitational or matter interactions, their dimensional reductions and their physical consequences?
destination.summary: A proposed organizing family spanning construction, completion, reduction, consistency tests and observables. Its branches retain different systems and perturbative orders. Adjacent questions remain accessible without becoming premises of the core family.

systems: Source-specified supergravity, string and M-theory effective actions across several dimensions
Four-dimensional Weyl supergravity, three-form gauge theories and supersymmetric Galileon interactions
Effective theories whose exact ∇⁴R⁴ coupling is studied for BPS information
targets: Supersymmetric higher-derivative invariants and auxiliary-field behavior
Reduced effective couplings and missing form-field terms
Duality, covariance, spectral and variational consistency
Black-object observables, holographic matching and signed BPS counts
regimes: Derivative order, loop order, dimension and field truncation remain source-specific
Four-derivative, R⁴ and ∇⁴R⁴ questions are separate branches
assumptions: Numerical membership is a retrieval proposal
Historical or conjectural source claims are context rather than established family premises
conventions: Action equivalence can depend on field redefinitions, total derivatives and Bianchi identities
A source-scoped singleton retains the exact supplied question and need not be atomic or cross-source unique
includes: Ordinary and pre-Swampland work when its scientific target fits
Six-dimensional matter and anomaly counterterms alongside four- and five-dimensional applications
Explicit alternate access for neighboring questions
excludes: A claim that all members ask the same scoped question
A universal four-dimensional, R⁴-only or Swampland premise
Automatic inclusion of every supersymmetry or compactification question in the higher-derivative core
Certification of complete actions or proofs from abstracts and introductory passages

sources.title: One loop superstring effective actions and d=4 supergravity

evidence.text: Which independent Weyl-quartic terms appear after reducing one-loop superstring effective actions to four dimensions, and how can their supersymmetrization coexist with chirality and R-symmetry restrictions?

sources.title: Higher-order string effective actions and off-shell $d=$4 supergravity

evidence.text: How do off-shell four-dimensional supergravity formulations support the supersymmetrization of string R^4 corrections, and which auxiliary fields remain algebraically eliminable? The review also considers implications for corrected black-hole entropy and attractors.

sources.title: F-theory at order $\alpha'^3$

evidence.text: Can auxiliary twelve-dimensional curvature package the α′³ graviton–axio-dilaton couplings of type IIB, and what genuinely N=1 contribution do varying axio-dilaton backgrounds produce in the four-dimensional gravitational Weyl factor?

sources.title: Higher derivatives in Type II and M-theory on Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Which two- and four-derivative effective couplings follow from Calabi–Yau threefold reductions of the known eight-derivative Type II and M-theory actions, and which additional form-field terms are required by lower-dimensional supersymmetry?

sources.title: Higher derivative three-form gauge theories and their supersymmetric extension

evidence.text: Which higher derivative interactions of four-dimensional three-form gauge fields avoid additional ghost or tachyon modes, and which boundary terms make their bosonic and supersymmetric variational problems consistent?

sources.title: Supersymmetry, T-duality and heterotic α′-corrections

evidence.text: How do supersymmetry and manifest T-duality constrain first-order heterotic α′ corrections, including the transformation rules, symmetry algebra and interactions of massless fermions?

sources.title: Higher-derivative supergravity, AdS$_{4}$ holography, and black holes

evidence.text: How do supersymmetric four-derivative interactions modify minimal gauged supergravity, AdS4 observables and black-hole thermodynamics, and can localization determine their coefficients and predict subleading large-N observables?

sources.title: Supersymmetry of higher-derivative supergravity in AdS4 holography

evidence.text: Which supersymmetric solutions survive the specified four-derivative corrections to minimal gauged supergravity, and can their renormalized action be expressed through fixed-point data while preserving the expected boundary supersymmetric invariance?

sources.title: AdS$_{5}$ holography and higher-derivative supergravity

evidence.text: How do supersymmetric four-derivative corrections modify minimal gauged 5d supergravity, holographic 4d conformal anomalies and supersymmetric black strings, and which bulk couplings can be inferred from microscopic SCFT data?

sources.title: Type IIA supergravity at one loop: α′$^{3}$ terms in the metric-dilaton-RR one-form sector

evidence.text: Which one-loop α′³ interactions of the type IIA metric, dilaton, and RR one-form follow from the eleven-dimensional pure-gravity eight-derivative action, and do their four-field amplitudes and K3 reductions satisfy the stated string-theory duality tests?

sources.title: One loop superstring effective actions and d=4 supergravity

evidence.text: Decompose the Weyl tensor into self-dual and anti-self-dual parts and translate to symmetric spinors. Restrict the contracted indices in the ten-dimensional curvature expressions to four dimensions, then express the results in the two-invariant basis and transform to Einstein frame.

sources.title: Higher-order string effective actions and off-shell $d=$4 supergravity

evidence.text: Reviewed tools include solving constrained superspace Bianchi identities off shell, chiral densities and projectors for invariant actions, and gauge completion to identify component fields by matching superspace and spacetime transformation laws.

sources.title: F-theory at order $\alpha'^3$

evidence.text: Promote ten-dimensional R4 contractions to curvature invariants of a block metric whose torus complex structure is τ. Hold the auxiliary torus volume fixed, allow only ten-dimensional derivatives, and retain the ten-dimensional integration measure.

sources.title: Higher derivatives in Type II and M-theory on Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Use Hodge decomposition and the ∂∂̄ lemma to separate harmonic and nonharmonic parts of c3 and express the metric correction through derivatives of a scalar. Tensor computations employ xAct/xTensor.

sources.title: Higher derivative three-form gauge theories and their supersymmetric extension

evidence.text: First-order formulations introduce an independent field strength and Lagrange multiplier to expose propagating modes. Auxiliary scalar or chiral superfields and diagonalization of kinetic terms diagnose the illustrative higher derivative instabilities.

sources.title: Supersymmetry, T-duality and heterotic α′-corrections

evidence.text: Expand the imported generalized Bergshoeff–de Roo construction: parameterize O(10,10+k) multiplets by O(10,10) fields and identify the generalized gauge connection with a fermion-corrected spin connection, and its gaugino with generalized gravitino curvature. Here k formally equals the dimension of O(1,9+k).

sources.title: Dimensional reduction of the M-theory Chern-Simons term at order <math display="inline"><msubsup><mo>ℓ</mo><mi>p</mi><mn>6</mn></msubsup></math>

evidence.text: What is the complete circle reduction of the eight-derivative M-theory Chern–Simons term, including gauge-invariant RR/NS-NS couplings beyond BR⁴, and does its selected six-dimensional reduction satisfy heterotic/type IIA S-duality?

sources.title: Aspects of Weyl Supergravity

evidence.text: Determine the propagating spectra of four-dimensional N=1,2,3,4 Weyl supergravities by taking the massless limit of Einstein–Weyl theories and accounting for enhanced gauge symmetries; investigate higher conformal tensors and possible holographic interpretations.

sources.title: Are genus corrections in effective actions invariant under Buscher rules?

evidence.text: Can the circle-reduced effective-action symmetry under derivative-corrected Buscher transformations be extended from tree level to higher genus, reproducing nonzero one-loop interactions known from S-matrix calculations?

sources.title: Tree-level R$^{4}$ correction from O(d, d): NS-NS five-point terms

evidence.text: Can cancellation of selected O(d,d)-violating terms in dimensional reduction determine a simpler completion of the tree-level R4 correction through five NS-NS fields, including the dilaton-sensitive terms omitted in the author's earlier treatment?

sources.title: Higher derivative couplings with multi-tensor multiplets in 6D supergravity, action and anomalies

evidence.text: Construct a proper action for six-dimensional (1,0) supergravity with multiple tensor multiplets and gauge anomalies, and obtain the leading supersymmetric gravitational Green–Schwarz curvature-squared counterterm with matter couplings.

sources.title: Higher derivative couplings of hypermultiplets

evidence.text: How can four-derivative hypermultiplet interactions restore local supersymmetry when six-dimensional Riemann-squared supergravity is coupled to hypermultiplets, and which couplings are compatible with the truncated heterotic construction?

sources.title: On extended supersymmetry of 4d Galileons and 3-brane effective actions

evidence.text: Which four-dimensional Galileon interactions admit extended supersymmetry in massless multiplets with spins at most one? The classification distinguishes two Galileons from a Galileon paired with an R-axion, and distinguishes isolated Galileon interactions from interactions coupled to DBI.

sources.title: On \alpha' corrections in N=1 F-theory compactifications

evidence.text: Which corrections to four-dimensional N=1 F-theory effective actions follow from classical reduction of the known purely gravitational eleven-dimensional R^4 terms, survive the F-theory limit, and admit a weakly coupled Type IIB interpretation?

sources.title: α′-corrections and their double formulation

evidence.text: How can gravitational α′ corrections to closed-string effective actions be expressed through duality-invariant double field theory (DFT), and how far can gauge/Lorentz identifications systematically generate higher-derivative actions and symmetry transformations?

sources.title: On anomaly - free supergravity as an effective string theory

evidence.text: Do the bosonic equations of anomaly-free supergravity satisfy, to all orders in α′, the differential consistency condition required of a candidate heterotic-string effective theory and of equations derivable from a generally covariant action?

sources.title: Exact $\nabla^4 R^4$ couplings and helicity supertraces

evidence.text: Does the exact ∇⁴R⁴ coupling encode signed 1/4-BPS state counts through its exponentially suppressed circle-decompactification corrections, particularly for D = 3, 4, 5?
